Are Lingala songs common in Congo? Congolese columnist Samuel Malonga Nkilutomba Luba Mabitidi noted that, although songs entirely performed in dialects are much less common than Lingala songs, they nevertheless maintain an important cultural presence. What is traditional Congolese music? Traditional Congolese music is characterized by anhemitonic pentatonic scales and a strong emphasis on polyphonic vocal textures, where overlapping voices blend without rigid melodic structures. While a basic melodic framework may be introduced, individual singers interpret it freely. When did dance become popular in Congo? By the late 1980s, dance in Congo had become increasingly fluid, with new styles emerging almost as quickly as the popularity of their predecessors waned. When did Congo rumba start? In 1934, Jean Réal, a French director of entertainment from Martinique, coined the term "Congo Rumba" when he founded a band of the same name in Brazzaville in 1938.
